acts.title: Act I: The Changing Security Arena
acts.scope: Evolution from narrow military frameworks to multidimensional threats like pandemics and cyber warfare

acts.title: Act II: Traditional Realist Security
acts.scope: Hobbesian state of nature, self-help system, military power, deterrence, and balance of power

acts.title: Act III: Liberal Institutionalism
acts.scope: Overcoming systemic anarchy through multilateral institutions, repeated interaction, and positive-sum trust

acts.title: Act IV: Constructivism & Security Communities
acts.scope: Social structures, Wendt's shared knowledge thesis, and transformation into peaceful security communities like NATO

acts.title: Act V: Critical Security Studies
acts.scope: Interrogating the state as a source of oppression and shifting the referent object to individuals and social groups

acts.title: Act VI: Feminist Security Theory
acts.scope: Unmasking gendered power relations and placing everyday structural and bodily violence at the center of security

acts.title: Act VII: Humanitarian Collapse in the DRC
acts.scope: Limits of military balancing exposed by 6 million civilian deaths, ethnic warfare, child soldiers, and mass rape

acts.title: Act VIII: Nuclear Governance & Proliferation
acts.scope: NPT 1968 architecture, dual-use technology dilemmas, North Korea treaty defection, and Iran inspection disputes

contrasts.axis: Referent object of security: state territorial survival versus individual and societal emancipation
Mechanism under anarchy: material balance and deterrence versus institutional rules and reciprocity
Spatial logic of world order: transnational open flows versus sovereign control of geographic space
Relation to non-proliferation regime: overt withdrawal and testing versus internal signatory inspection disputes

nodes.title: Global Security Dynamics
nodes.subtitle: From Sovereign Territorial Defense to Multidimensional and Human Security
bullets: Post-Cold War threats transcend sovereign borders and expose limits of conventional military power
Security debates contest whose protection matters: the ruling state or individual human beings

nodes.title: Act I: Changing Arena
nodes.subtitle: Multidimensional Vectors and Borderless Threats
bullets: End of superpower confrontation unveiled complex non-military systemic vulnerabilities
Transnational dangers require analytical frameworks beyond national defense

nodes.title: Multidimensional Security
nodes.subtitle: Broadened conceptualization spanning political, economic, societal, and ecological spheres
bullets: Recognizes human vulnerability extends across societal, economic, and environmental domains
Expands the level of security analysis from the nation-state to regional and global collectives

nodes.title: Transnational Interdependent Threats
nodes.subtitle: Borderless dangers evading sovereign territorial containment
bullets: Pandemics, climate collapse, cyber warfare, and terrorism operate across national boundaries
Tanks and ballistic missiles provide zero defense against systemic planetary disruptions

nodes.title: Act II: Realist Security
nodes.subtitle: Hobbesian Anarchy and the Self-Help State
bullets: Sovereign nation-states operate as primary actors in an anarchic international system
Absence of overarching global authority compels self-help reliance on military power

nodes.title: State-Centric Defense
nodes.subtitle: Realist paradigm prioritizing territorial integrity and state survival
bullets: Views world politics as an anarchic Hobbesian state of nature where power dictates survival
Considers rival powerful nation-states as the foremost existential danger to sovereignty

nodes.title: Balancing and Deterrence
nodes.subtitle: Equilibrium mechanisms preventing hegemon dominance
bullets: States build offensive and defensive arsenals while constructing counter-alliances
International stability is maintained solely when no single power achieves hegemonic status

nodes.title: Act III: Liberal Institutions
nodes.subtitle: Overcoming Anarchy Through Multilateral Rules
bullets: International institutions actively mitigate anarchy by structuring state cooperation
Rule-bound multilateralism enables states to resolve security rivalries peacefully

nodes.title: Institutional Security Regimes
nodes.subtitle: Multilateral frameworks transforming anarchic competition
bullets: Bodies like the United Nations, WTO, and NATO establish binding rules for interaction
Channel state self-interest into managed, collaborative governance producing positive-sum gains

nodes.title: Iterated Reciprocity & Trust
nodes.subtitle: Repeated diplomatic interaction reducing transactional costs
bullets: Institutions provide continuous information and transparency to reduce strategic miscalculation
Repeated interactions foster mutual trust, internalizing cooperative norms over time

nodes.title: Act IV: Constructivism
nodes.subtitle: Social Structures and Shared Identities
bullets: International structures are socially constituted through knowledge rather than material arms
Evolution of state identities can replace zero-sum rivalry with non-violent norms

nodes.title: Social Security Architecture
nodes.subtitle: Wendtian thesis on the social constitution of world politics
bullets: Anarchy does not dictate war; state interactions determine whether anarchy is hostile or cooperative
Shared meanings, discourse, and institutional socialization define national interests

nodes.title: Transnational Security Communities
nodes.subtitle: Pluralistic groupings where war becomes socially unthinkable
bullets: Member states share collective democratic identity and dependable expectations of peaceful change
Exemplified by NATO allies who no longer perceive each other as potential military threats

nodes.title: Act V: Critical Studies
nodes.subtitle: Interrogating Power and State Oppression
bullets: Emerged in the 1980s and 90s to challenge state-centric orthodoxy and militarism
Exposes how existing power hierarchies manufacture structural insecurity for populations

nodes.title: Critical Security Paradigm
nodes.subtitle: Shifting the referent object from the sovereign state to human beings
bullets: Broadens security inquiry to individuals, vulnerable communities, and marginalized social groups
Aims to transform unjust social hierarchies and achieve genuine human emancipation

nodes.title: State as Oppressive Source
nodes.subtitle: Domestic authoritarianism and human rights violations
bullets: Authoritarian regimes frequently inflict far greater violence on citizens than foreign invaders
Focusing exclusively on state survival legitimizes regime oppression under the guise of order

nodes.title: Act VI: Feminist Security
nodes.subtitle: Gendered Hierarchies and Everyday Violence
bullets: Questions foundational patriarchal assumptions underpinning traditional state security
Demonstrates national and global security fundamentally depends on the safety of women

nodes.title: Feminist Security Lens
nodes.subtitle: Centering gender subordination and women's agency in security analysis
bullets: Exposes traditional security discourse as exclusively focused on elite masculine experiences
Recognizes women not merely as victims, but as active political agents transforming peace

nodes.title: Everyday Gendered Insecurity
nodes.subtitle: Pervasive structural and domestic threats hidden from military agendas
bullets: Highlights intimate partner violence, rape, honor killings, and female infanticide as security crises
Addresses systematic economic inequality, lack of healthcare access, and human trafficking

nodes.title: Globalization Flow Model
nodes.subtitle: De-territorialized exchange of capital, goods, and transnational ideas
bullets: Argues market integration and borderless communication generate mutual interdependence
Reduces traditional incentives for territorial conquest in an interconnected world

nodes.title: Resurgent Geopolitics
nodes.subtitle: Strategic competition for physical space, resources, and geographic chokepoints
bullets: National and imperial strategies prioritize dominion over vital maritime corridors and minerals
Reflected in great power strategic realignments toward Pacific and regional theater dominance

nodes.title: Act VII: DRC Case Study
nodes.subtitle: The Human Catastrophe of Regionalized War
bullets: Conflict (1996–2013) following Rwandan genocide spillover became Africa's world war
Exposes complete collapse of traditional balance of power concepts in intrastate crises

nodes.title: DRC Regionalized Warfare
nodes.subtitle: Mass civilian mortality and multi-state proxy interventions
bullets: Spillover of 1994 Rwandan genocide drew Rwanda, Uganda, Burundi, and Angola into conflict
Resulted in an estimated 6 million deaths, primarily from famine, disease, and societal collapse

nodes.title: Limits of Military Paradigms
nodes.subtitle: Inability of conventional armies to halt societal atrocity
bullets: Systemic deployment of mass rape and child soldier recruitment weaponized human insecurity
Proves true security requires human rights, economic development, and freedom from fear

nodes.title: Act VIII: Nuclear Governance
nodes.subtitle: Treaty Frameworks, Dual-Use Tech, and Defection
bullets: Management of catastrophic nuclear arms balances non-proliferation against civilian energy rights
Regime credibility faces severe strain from clandestine enrichment and unilateral exit

nodes.title: NPT 1968 Architecture
nodes.subtitle: The cornerstone multilateral bargain restricting nuclear weapons acquisition
bullets: Recognizes 5 nuclear weapon states while legally barring all non-nuclear signatories from acquisition
Provides peaceful civilian nuclear assistance under International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) monitoring

nodes.title: Dual-Use Fuel Dilemma
nodes.subtitle: Civilian enrichment technology diversion into weapons-grade fissile material
bullets: Uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing for electricity share identical technological pathways with bombs
Creates severe proliferation risks even when civilian nuclear facilities operate under safeguard protocols

nodes.title: North Korea Defection
nodes.subtitle: Agreed Framework collapse, treaty withdrawal, and overt nuclear tests
bullets: Shut down plutonium reactor under 1994 Agreed Framework before withdrawing from NPT in 2003
Conducted multiple nuclear detonations starting in 2006, defying diplomatic denuclearization efforts

nodes.title: Iran Compliance Dispute
nodes.subtitle: Undeclared enrichment controversies under sustained IAEA monitoring
bullets: Maintains NPT signatory status while asserting sovereign rights to civilian energy enrichment
IAEA identified potential military dimensions, triggering multilateral sanctions and verification talks
